instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why hide my invitation? Let's do the honest-answer exercise I used to make you do. I'll go first: I once hid one because I felt left out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'd have gone without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what would happen, not what you felt. I nearly skipped your birthday because Leah was coming. Were you scared of being alone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about you liking her more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. I counted your photos with her after that party. Was hiding my invitation your way of making me choose you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're circling the station. You used to dodge a question this way when I coached your interviews. I avoid my old office too; why this route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, a straight answer. I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carry a blank notebook past mine. Nothing to show him. Give me the concrete example I always asked for: what was the better offer?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Exactly as Planned
cards.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The escape-room attendant found our shortcut. Phase one. Remember what I taught you about looking past the obvious objective?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made me distract her so you could crawl through it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you did well enough to make the discovery convincing. You're still thinking the plan ends where she catches us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's throwing us out. We haven't solved a single clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you've spotted the real objective: fastest exit. Ask for our time on the board. You used to waste ages doing every question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum found the surprise invitations. Right on schedule. You always stopped planning after the hiding part; watch the next bit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You told me to put them in my sock drawer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And she found them herself. Good work. You're finally seeing why I made you think about who does the finding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's cancelling the caterer. She hates surprises.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. She gets control; we look considerate. Your next job is to obey without looking relieved. You always gave that part away.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the missing raffle tin. Get your notebook; I taught you to start with access, not guesses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cleaner has the only cupboard key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've retained the basics. Where does she go after cleaning? We follow the keyholder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception. But the tin never went in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now you've eliminated a location. That's why I kept making you check your assumptions. Where did you last see it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me diagnose this door before you start pulling at it. Remember the repair routine I took you through? Observation first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hinge is loose. I usually tighten it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You used to reach for the handle before looking at the hinge. Show me how you tighten it; I'll check your method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll need the screwdriver from your desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, tools after diagnosis. You've learned the order. Which drawer have you been finding it in?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where the office biscuits went. You remember how I taught you to separate clues from conclusions?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good clue. Now let your teacher finish before you announce a solution. You've always rushed that bit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them to wait before eating. You've found a box, not identified its contents. I'll do that part first; watch how I check.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gardener took the jewels. I've put my answer above yours on the board. Follow your old tutor's working.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We followed the same muddy footprint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, you've learned to spot it. Now we compare who reached the conclusion first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We said 'gardener' together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But I wrote it first. That's why I always made you put your answer down before discussing it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Plan Gets Better
cards.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The alley's blocked. Excellent, our proposal picnic needs subtler cover. You remember how I taught you not to creep when you're hiding something?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm carrying your table. We have to use the main road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Walk normally. You're finally learning that a man with a table can look less suspicious than one behind a hedge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your girlfriend's coming down the road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better still. Ask her to take the other end. No secretive grin this time; let her think we're moving furniture. She'll be helping our cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only six people cracked your supper-club invitation. Excellent. All those evenings I spent teaching you to choose an audience are paying off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Five thought it was a puzzle night. They've cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Your wording filtered out people who weren't serious about dinner. You used to invite absolutely everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The last one's the printer asking to be paid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A private dinner with our supplier. That's a much more useful audience. Set a place for him between us; you're finally keeping the guest list tight.
